# 3.1 Recursion, backtracking, pruning

Phase 3 (Recursion to dynamic programming), target rating 1500–1900. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Generate every valid object (`generate-all`)

Recursively generate all combinations, permutations, or partitions that satisfy the constraints.

**Works because:** The number of valid objects is itself small enough to list.

### Place with checks (`constraint-placement`)

Fill positions one at a time (queens, grid puzzles), checking constraints after each placement and undoing on return.

**Works because:** A partial assignment that already breaks a constraint can be rejected without extending it.

### Cut hopeless branches (`bound-pruning`)

Abandon a branch when its cost so far plus an optimistic estimate cannot beat the best answer found.

**Works because:** The estimate never overstates what the rest of the branch can achieve.

### Split into two halves (`meet-in-middle`)

n ≈ 40: enumerate 2^(n/2) choices for each half and combine the two lists with sorting and searching.

**Works because:** The objective decomposes into a part from each half that can be combined after sorting one list.
